title: Auth reset password
summary: 'Set a new password' page paired with a reset link. Composes the auth-reset-password block; the opaque token (typically from a `?token=…` URL parameter) is forwarded verbatim to adapter.resetPassword.
brief: Ship a reset-password page that accepts a token (from URL params), takes a new password + confirm, and calls my auth library's reset endpoint.

steps.reason: The page-level block — wires confirm-match validation, the opaque token, error display, and success redirect.
Accessible labels for the password fields

checklist.check: Read `?token=…` in your route (Next.js: server-component `searchParams`; client: useSearchParams) and pass it as the `token` prop. The block treats the value as opaque.
Pass an AuthAdapter via the `adapter` prop with `resetPassword` implemented.
Validate the token inside `adapter.resetPassword`, never inside the block. Surface expiry / mismatch via `{ ok: false, error }`.
Keep `passwordMinLength` aligned with auth-sign-up-card so users don't face a stricter rule on reset than they did at signup.
Wire `onSuccess` to navigate to `/sign-in` (or call your auto-sign-in flow). The block does not navigate by itself.

[AuthResetPassword] Avoid: Hard-coding `token` to an empty string when the URL param is absent — the block surfaces a 'link is invalid or expired' error, but the consumer should redirect to /forgot-password instead. Read searchParams in the route and pass it through.

[AuthResetPassword] Avoid: Validating the token shape inside the block — the block treats it as opaque on purpose. Validate inside adapter.resetPassword and surface the error via { ok: false, error }.

[AuthResetPassword] Avoid: Skipping onSuccess and relying on adapter.redirect alone — the redirect is informational; the consumer's onSuccess handler is what actually navigates after the password is saved.

[AuthResetPassword] Avoid: Setting passwordMinLength inconsistently between sign-up and reset-password — keep them aligned (both default to 8) so users don't hit a stricter check on reset than they did on signup.

[AuthResetPassword] A11y: Both inputs use autoComplete='new-password' and have explicit Label htmlFor pairing. The password helper text is wired via aria-describedby. Submit button uses the canonical loading prop (sets aria-busy + disabled). Errors render in an Alert with role='alert' so they're announced.
[Input] Avoid: Missing associated Label element for accessibility
[Input] Avoid: Using type='number' without min/max constraints
[Input] Avoid: Not providing placeholder text for context
[Input] A11y: Always pair with a Label using htmlFor/id. Consider aria-describedby for helper text or error messages.
[Label] Avoid: Forgetting to set htmlFor matching the input's id
[Label] Avoid: Using Label for non-form text content
[Label] Avoid: Nesting interactive elements inside Label
[Label] A11y: Clicking the label focuses the associated control. Automatically communicates the label to screen readers. Use htmlFor/id pairing, not nesting.
[Button] Avoid: Nesting interactive elements inside asChild button
[Button] Avoid: Using — breaks middle-click, cmd-click, and right-click → 'open in new tab', and skips the browser history entry
[Button] Avoid: Using <Button variant='destructive'> for recoverable actions like 'Reset filters' — reserve destructive for delete/archive/leave; use 'secondary' or 'ghost' for resets
[Button] Avoid: Using <Button size='icon'> without an aria-label — screen readers have nothing to announce; always pair icon-only buttons with aria-label or visible text
[Button] A11y: Automatically handles focus ring, disabled state, and aria attributes. Icon-only buttons MUST have aria-label. Loading state automatically sets disabled.
[Alert] Avoid: Using destructive for non-error messages
[Alert] Avoid: Missing AlertTitle (reduces scannability)
[Alert] Avoid: Stacking multiple Alerts on the same page instead of grouping
[Alert] A11y: Root renders role='alert' so screen readers announce it. For non-urgent info banners consider role='status' or aria-live='polite' via className overrides.
